issues.legal_issue: A person not shown to have been born in the country may be a citizen there at the relevant time by having a domicile of choice there and being ordinarily resident there for the required preceding period.
material_facts: The election challenge alleged that the successful candidate was not a citizen and therefore lacked the constitutional qualification to be elected.

The Court proceeded on the assumption that the candidate was not born in the country, and the finding that he had been ordinarily resident there for five years immediately before the relevant time was not challenged.

Before the relevant time, the candidate had lived and managed extensive family and personal properties in the country, acquired property there, and established his home and family there; he also held a passport identifying him as Indian.
The candidate’s subsequent life in the country included marriage, raising children, civic participation, and political activity.
issues.conclusion: The candidate had acquired a domicile of choice in the country before the relevant time and satisfied the ordinary-residence requirement; he was therefore a citizen at that time and duly qualified for election.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 5(c) of the Constitution, citizenship requires domicile in the territory of India and ordinary residence there for the five years immediately preceding the commencement of the Constitution. A domicile of choice is acquired through residence in a country with a present, fixed intention to make it one’s permanent home; the intention required is permanent residence, not an intention to abandon one’s nationality. The party asserting a change from domicile of origin bears the burden of proving it. The Court applied Udny v. Udny, L.R. 1 H.L. Sc. 441, and Doucet v. Geoghegan, 9 Ch. Div. 441, and also referred to Winans v. Attorney-General, [1904] A.C. 287, and Munro v. Munro, 7 C.I. & Fin. 876. Article 173 makes citizenship a qualification for election to the State Legislature.

rule.if: election_qualification_challenge and (birth_in_country_unproven or not_birth_in_country) and ordinary_residence_for_required_period and residence_in_country and settled_intention_to_make_country_permanent_home

predicates.election_qualification_challenge: A proceeding challenged a person's election on the ground that the person lacked the required citizenship qualification.
predicates.birth_in_country_unproven: The person's birth in the country was not established.
predicates.not_birth_in_country: The person was treated as not having been born in the country.
predicates.ordinary_residence_for_required_period: The person was ordinarily resident in the country throughout the required period immediately before the relevant time.
predicates.residence_in_country: The person lived in the country and established a home there.
predicates.settled_intention_to_make_country_perman: The person formed a deliberate, settled intention to make the country a permanent home for himself or herself and the family.

issues.definition: When an election-qualification challenge concerns a person whose birth in the country is unproven or did not occur there, the person is a citizen at the relevant time if the person was ordinarily resident there for the required period, lived there, and had formed a settled intention to make it a permanent home.

issues.legal_issue: Conduct and circumstances occurring after the time for which domicile is being determined are relevant evidence of a person's intention at that time.
material_facts: The Court had to determine whether the candidate had acquired a domicile of choice before the Constitution came into force.
The candidate's conduct and activities after that time included marriage, family life, civic involvement, and political activity in the country.
The Court considered later conduct relevant, while deciding the question mainly in light of the candidate's conduct and activities before the relevant time.
issues.conclusion: Conduct and activities after the relevant time may be considered, with appropriate weight, in determining a person's domicile at that time.
issues.legal_principle: In determining domicile at a particular time, conduct and circumstances before, at, and after that time may be considered, with their relative evidentiary weight. The Court relied on In re Grove, Vaucher v. The Solicitor to the Treasury, (1889) 40 Ch. D. 216.

predicates.domicile_determination: A court is determining a person's domicile at a particular time.
predicates.conduct_after_relevant_time: The person's conduct or activities occurred after the time for which domicile is being determined.

issues.definition: When a court determines domicile at a particular time, conduct occurring afterward is relevant evidence of that domicile.
